## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This Phase 3 RRMM trial needs to demonstrate how the proteasome inhibitor affects patient-experienced bone pain, treatment tolerability, and physical function preservation through validated PRO endpoints positioned for regulatory acceptance.

**Key challenge:** No single instrument covers disease-related bone pain — the most clinically important domain in multiple myeloma — requiring either the EORTC QLQ-C30/MY20 pair (50 items) or acceptance of domain gaps in the measurement strategy.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-MY20 with QLQ-C30 for comprehensive coverage (scores 68/100), EQ-5D-5L for HTA utility requirements (NICE/ICER mandated), and BFI for fatigue sensitivity (score 68/100, validated MCID available [IR-001]).

**Critical gap:** If EQ-5D-5L is excluded, NICE will not accept cost-effectiveness evidence, preventing UK reimbursement regardless of other PRO findings.

## Key Observations

• **Endpoint positioning precedent:** In 141 KG trials, 132 (93%) used PRO endpoints as secondary, 9 (6%) exploratory, and none as primary — indicating proteasome inhibitor trials position PRO findings as supportive evidence rather than primary regulatory claims [TI-001-005].

• **Domain coverage challenge:** The EORTC QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale captures bone pain comprehensively with 6 pain-specific items (bone aches, back pain, hip pain, arm/shoulder pain, chest pain, activity-related pain increase), making it the only validated instrument addressing this core FDA domain [EORTC QLQ-MY20 specimen](https://www.eortc.org/app/uploads/sites/2/2018/08/Specimen-MY20-English.pdf).

• **MCID validation available:** The QLQ-MY20 has established anchor-based MIDs: Disease Symptoms (10 points), Side Effects of Treatment (10 points), Future Perspective (9 points), and Body Image (13 points) from mixed-methods validation in MM patients [PMC6852250](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6852250/) — making it interpretation-ready for regulatory submissions.

• **Calibrated SOA opportunity:** 77 KG trials used QLQ-MY20 subscales rather than the full instrument — suggesting expert consideration of a Disease Symptoms + Side Effects focused approach could reduce burden from 50 items (C30+MY20) to approximately 25-30 items while preserving core domains.

• **HTA utility requirement:** NICE explicitly mandates EQ-5D for cost-effectiveness analysis — Table 3 shows EQ-5D-5L achieves this requirement with established regulatory acceptance, making its inclusion non-negotiable for UK market access regardless of other PRO selections.

• **Regulatory modernisation context:**  FDA released draft guidance in January 2026 on MRD endpoints for multiple myeloma accelerated approval , signaling agency focus on efficacy biomarkers rather than PRO-based primary endpoints — supporting the secondary positioning observed in historical trials.

## Comparator Analysis

No COMP-XXX entries exist in the evidence block — expert should review recent FDA and EMA medical reviews for proteasome inhibitor submissions.

However, the KG trial evidence shows consistent proteasome inhibitor sensitivity: **TOURMALINE-MM3 (ixazomib)** detected significant improvements across all QLQ-C30 functional domains and QLQ-MY20 subscales (p<0.05) [TI-003], while **A.R.R.O.W. (carfilzomib)** showed significant improvements in QLQ-MY20 disease symptoms and side effects (p<0.01) [TI-004]. This supports EORTC instruments as validated change-detection tools for this drug class.

**ENDEAVOR (carfilzomib)** demonstrated significant FACT/GOG-NTX improvements (p<0.001) specifically for neuropathy endpoints [TI-005] — indicating proteasome inhibitor trials successfully detect treatment-related neuropathy changes, relevant if peripheral neuropathy is a differentiated safety signal for the current compound.

Based on comparator evidence, **EORTC QLQ-MY20** has the strongest signal of change in this indication because it consistently demonstrated significant improvements across multiple proteasome inhibitor trials with different patient populations and treatment combinations.

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Domain coverage strategy:** Accept EORTC QLQ-C30/MY20 pair (50 items, comprehensive) versus targeted subscale selection (25-30 items, domain gaps in symptomatic AEs).

2. **Bone pain measurement approach:** Rely on QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale as the sole bone pain measure, or add a dedicated pain instrument like BPI-SF for enhanced pain granularity.

3. **Neuropathy endpoint inclusion:** Whether FACT/GOG-NTX merits inclusion based on compound-specific neuropathy risk profile versus KG evidence of carfilzomib neuropathy signal detection.

4. **Assessment timing optimisation:** Schedule aligned with proteasome inhibitor dosing patterns (typically weekly/biweekly cycles) while avoiding assessment fatigue in an elderly, frail patient population.

5. **Regulatory positioning hierarchy:** Which single QLQ-MY20 subscale (Disease Symptoms versus Side Effects) to position as the alpha-controlled secondary endpoint if survival endpoints (PFS/OS) achieve significance.
